neighbours.label: the universal or negative indefinites everywhere, anywhere, nowhere, everything, anything (often before 'else')
fire: You could not ask for friendlier staff anywhere else on the coast.
This orchid grows wild here and nowhere else on the island.
As with everything else, the cost of timber went up.
Just as everywhere, the shops close early on Sundays.
The bread here is better than anything else in the bakery.
Like anywhere, the old town can get crowded in summer.
She loved him more than anything else in her life.
Like everything, this habit takes time to learn.
quiet: You could not ask for friendlier staff at the other hotels on the coast.
This orchid grows wild on the island and in a few nearby valleys.
As with most materials, the cost of timber went up.
Just as in Spain, the shops close early on Sundays.
The bread here is better than the cakes in the bakery.
Like many ports, the old town can get crowded in summer.
She loved him more than her own family in her life.
Like any skill, this habit takes time to learn.
